posts.author: whtdragon
posts.body:
Christmas comes early this year and I've got one doozy of a present for everyone here. I noticed when looking at the default resources in MV that there was an unusually small amount of animals--a smaller amount then most of the other RPG makers, and that will simply not do. I took a look at every other RPG maker's animals and I decided to
remake them all for MV.
I then also added some new animals that I felt like should be givens for any typical game. I tried to keep them faithful to the MV style, and there are a few I'm not completely satisfied with, and I will try and fix when I can.
Current count of unique animal sprites: 50+ (s-so many!)
​
I was also
given
a suggestion by
Skysurfer
about running horses. I was not going to do that at first but then I said "challange excepted" and well now we have running horses. (again trying to keep to the MV style)
DISCLAIMER:
the running horse animation IS 4 frames, so you will either need a plugin for extra frames or you will need to use some other method of using 4 frames in your animations, but it should be usable. Apologies that I could not bring it down to the default three frames, I really did try! But it just was not working like I wanted it to. Alternatively, they can be used in RPG maker XP.  For the sake of information, the frames are 64x57, slightly bigger then the original sprite.
Terms:
As these are (mostly) edits of MV's sprites, you will need a legal copy of RPG maker MV

I almost didn't make it a completely new animal on it's own instead trying to work it in as a different wolf or coyote, but it ended up being more of a general purpose "wild dog" that could work as a dingo, a jackal, a coyote, or just another type of dog. I will probably be making some new recolors of them eventually, since I'm not super satisfied with what's there right now.
The bison and musk ox are somewhat interesting as I actually had a really hard time making the original bull/cow faces, and while experimenting with the faces, some of the experiments ended up being those two, so they've been in my list of things to make for awhile, I just hadn't gotten around to finishing them up until recently.

new update u w o7 I wanted to get these out before my birthday tomorrow, sooo consider this an early birthday surprise!
I'm quickly finding out that large sprites are taking up a LOT more time, especially if they're not straight up edits.
On Kirin/Qilin, Carbuncle, the Kraken and other such things: I kept them fairly generic, and in the case of Kirin and Carbuncle, I mostly based their designs off of RPG maker 2003's battle sprites, though I did leave alternative color pallets from more popular variants like the final fantasy series, and other variant colors for other potential uses. Kirin even comes with two versions, one with a single horn and one with traditional antler horns.  I do not particularly like making sprites that are very obviously from a specific game or movie since those can be very specific and it can end up being a lot of work I could be using on more interesting or sought after things, so I don't think you'll be expecting anything like that from me anytime soon. (though if enough people say so, I might do a chocobo sometime I dunno)
The Kraken is of course mostly just a boss-esk sprite with separate tentacles for moving around and animating. Nothing too impressive about him other then he's kind of animate-able -- I liked the big bad boss's sprite from RPG XP that had his arms separated out to do the same thing so I imagine anyone that's messed with XP any will appreciate that at least.
The giant chicken sprite was made out of a need to get the cockatrice sprite working. I could have made the cockatrice a simple chicken edit, but I wanted something bigger. YAY EXTRA EFFORT~ but I thought it'd be amusing to have this big fat chicken you could have on screen too! It is also pretty much an upscaled version of the default, an easy thing to with pixel resizing~ (that and the larger sprite makes them out to look all rolly polly and having a waddling round fat monster that can turn you into stone amuses me)
Anyways I probably won't be uploading anything for a few days ~ I do have some other stuff planned that I do want to upload that isn't animals though, at least one of which is close enough to getting finished, so maybe I'll get to upload it and something else sometime next week.
Enjoy for now u w o~!

posts.author: Niten Ichi Ryu
posts.body:
any RPG maker RTP is NOT free to download, it's available for download, but limited in use to legal owners.
If a resource is an edit from MV RTP, yes you need to own MV to use it.
If a resource is an edit from VX ACE RTP, yes you need to own VX ACE to use it.
And if you own MV and VX ACE, you have a license to use ACE RTP in MV and Vice Versa.
that simple logic applies to all makers.

The method I use for resizing though unfortunately pretty much requires an old outdated program no one uses anymore /)- 3 -; but I can try to describe it and maybe you can find a way on another program. I use Paintshop pro 7and in it, when you go to to resize there's an option to do a "pixel resize" in it, which means it'll just resize based on pixels rather then try to resize with antialias, making the sprites fuzzy or blurry. Pixel resize does leave the images looking pretty jagged and distorted, but so much easier to work with when you're working in sprites.

I believe Gimp has a similar feature called "scale image" and under "quality" you select none, which should give you similar results but-- mm don't quote me on that one.
